assertions.name: all_two_crossing_candidates_share_one_writhe
assertions.source: every candidate has writhe +2, so ANY writhe-based normalisation of the Markov trace is identical across them. Without this the trace comparison below would be confounded by the normalisation rather than measuring the link

assertions.name: the_four_tied_candidates_are_four_distinct_links
assertions.source: 4 distinct (tr_p, tr_n) pairs over 4 candidates at equal writhe. The Markov trace at an admissible z is a link invariant after writhe normalisation (conjugation invariance is automatic for a trace; stabilisation gives the z factor), so equal writhe plus different trace is SUFFICIENT for different closures

assertions.name: reordering_ALONE_changes_the_link
assertions.source: sigma_1 sigma_0 and sigma_0 sigma_1 have the SAME letter multiset and the SAME writhe and differ only in order; their traces differ by 0.0677559 (proton) and 0.0142094 (neutron). The closure is order-SENSITIVE

assertions.name: every_letter_sum_functional_is_structurally_barred_here
assertions.source: a sum over letters is constant on the permutation orbit of a letter multiset, and the closure is not -- so NO functional of the multiset alone can select among these candidates, for any q and any coefficients. This upgrades the E_cross tie from an observation to a scope-(b) exclusion of the whole letter-sum class, invariant named: order-sensitivity of the closure

assertions.name: an_isotopy_class_energy_is_NOT_barred
assertions.source: the candidates are distinct isotopy classes, so the O'Hara/Moebius INFIMUM -- which is a function of the class -- takes potentially different values on them. Green light: the Bring->O'Hara route is not stillborn on discriminability. It does NOT follow that the energy would in fact separate them; a prune establishes only that it is not excluded

description: A formalize-first prune run BEFORE the Bring->O'Hara bridge is built. Moebius energy is a property of an embedding, not a knot invariant; the invariant is the infimum over the isotopy class, so a selection rule built on it can only separate candidates that are DIFFERENT LINKS. Tested without any embedding: the Markov trace at the admissible z_D is a link invariant once normalised by writhe, and all four two-crossing gluon candidates have writhe +2 -- identical normalisation -- yet give four DISTINCT (tr_p, tr_n) pairs. The sharpest case is sigma_1 sigma_0 vs sigma_0 sigma_1: same letter multiset, same writhe, differing only in ORDER, and the traces differ. They are different links, so an isotopy-class energy is NOT structurally barred from breaking the tie -- green light for the route. It also upgrades the E_cross failure from an observation to a scope-(b) exclusion of the whole letter-sum CLASS: a sum over letters is constant on the permutation orbit of a multiset and the closure is not.

method.why_no_embedding_needed: Moebius energy needs an embedding, but the QUESTION -- are these the same link? -- is answerable with a link invariant alone
method.invariant: Markov trace at z_D, normalised by writhe
method.admissibility: z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) is an admissible Markov parameter under convention D
method.direction: distinguishing is SUFFICIENT, not necessary -- convention D annihilates the (1,1,1) block, so this truncated invariant may fail to separate some different links. The asymmetry is in the safe direction for a prune

verdict.letter_sum_class: scope-(b) excluded -- constant on the permutation orbit while the closure is not
verdict.isotopy_class_energy: NOT excluded -- green light for the Bring->O'Hara route

scope.class: (b) structural for the letter-sum exclusion; (a) for the green light
not_claimed: that the O'Hara/Moebius energy would in fact separate them
that the bridge is easy -- it still needs a canonical embedding or the minimiser
that any candidate should be adopted
scope.no_selection_by_accuracy: no Q_beta appears in this probe at all
